skill.name: safe-refactor
skill.description: Restructure code while preserving behavior. Use for extraction, consolidation, ownership moves, or cleanup where verification must bracket structural edits.
skill.summary: Guide focused refactors with verification before and after each structural change.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by a normal refactoring constraint in SKILL.md. No malicious intent, unsafe system access, or prompt injection was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid dependency or configuration growth without correctness need.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 14 only advises avoiding unnecessary dependency or configuration growth during refactoring. It does not request system reconnaissance, configuration discovery, or privileged access.

content.value_statement: Structural code changes can introduce subtle regressions and expand scope. This skill defines behavior boundaries and brackets focused refactors with verification.
actual_capabilities: Defines the behavior that a refactor must preserve.
Separates structural work from feature changes.
Plans one ownership-boundary move at a time.
Preserves interfaces, failures, ordering, and compatibility unless scope says otherwise.
Requires equivalent verification before and after structural edits.
limitations: Does not provide language-specific refactoring commands.
Does not create tests when no verification method exists.
Does not approve intentional behavior or interface changes.
Depends on available builds, tests, or other observable proof.

use_cases.title: Extract a Shared Module
use_cases.description: Plan a focused extraction while preserving callers, error behavior, and test results.

use_cases.title: Move Component Ownership
use_cases.description: Transfer one responsibility between packages while keeping public interfaces stable.

use_cases.title: Review Maintenance Changes
use_cases.description: Check whether a cleanup remains structural and includes equivalent verification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-refactor to plan this cleanup. Identify preserved behavior, the smallest structural change, and verification before and after the edit.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear plan for a contained cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Repeated Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the repeated logic into one owner. Preserve interfaces, failures, ordering, and compatibility. Keep each intermediate state buildable and testable.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants to consolidate duplicated behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Move an Ownership Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Move this responsibility from the current module to the target module. Separate feature changes and verify every affected public contract.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is reorganizing responsibilities across modules.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Staged Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Design staged changes for this cross-package refactor. Define invariants, compatibility constraints, rollback points, and equivalent proof for every stage.
prompt_templates.scenario: A senior engineer is planning a high-impact structural change.

output_examples.input: Move validation from the controller into the domain service without changing API behavior.
output: Boundary: preserve response status, error messages, validation order, and public service signatures.
Sequence: characterize current behavior, move validation, keep the controller adapter, then remove duplication.
Verification: run the same controller and service tests before and after each step.

output_examples.input: Consolidate duplicate cache invalidation logic used by two modules.
output: Boundary: preserve invalidation timing, key format, failure handling, and call order.
Sequence: introduce one owner, migrate one caller, verify, then migrate the second caller.
Stop condition: both callers use the shared owner and existing behavior remains proven.

best_practices: Record observable behavior and verification commands before editing.
Move one responsibility at a time and keep every state testable.
Run the same proof after changes and stop when the requested structure is achieved.
anti_patterns: Mixing new features with structural changes.
Changing public contracts without explicit scope.
Adding dependencies or configuration without a correctness need.

faq.question: What counts as a safe refactor?
faq.answer: A safe refactor changes structure while preserving explicitly defined observable behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: It guides an agent through scoped structural edits when code and verification tools are available.

faq.question: Can I change an API during the refactor?
faq.answer: Only when the API change is explicitly scoped. Otherwise, public interfaces should remain stable.

faq.question: What verification should I use?
faq.answer: Use existing tests, builds, static checks, or focused behavior checks that cover the preserved boundary.

faq.question: Can this skill add dependencies?
faq.answer: It discourages dependency growth unless a dependency is required for correctness.

faq.question: When should the refactor stop?
faq.answer: Stop when behavior matches the baseline and the requested structure is achieved.
